newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese workers demand 20 percent wage increase.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese workers demand 20 percent wage increase.

text.p: Lebanon's General Labour Confederation (CGTL) has demanded a wage increase of at least 20 percent for public and private sector workers backdated to January 1, 1997.

"We demand a wage correction of at least 20 percent... for all workers and employees of the private and public sector," the CGTL's executive council said in a statement published on Friday in Beirut newspapers.
Billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri's government granted private-sector workers a graded pay rise of between five and 20 percent last May, but the CGTL dismissed it as insufficient.

The CGTL, which groups most of Lebanon's 350,000 private-sector workers, also asked the government to launch a positive dialogue with the workers over their demands. There are some 120,000 public-sector workers in Lebanon.
The CGTL said the government must follow an austerity programme, adding that "useless spending consumed about 15 percent of the public budget".

"We demand curbing the debt policy, especially the foreign debt, because it threatens the independence and free will of the country," CGTL said in the statement after a meeting of its executive council.
"The public debt is truly a big time-bomb that threatens the basis of stability and the possibility of recovery," it added.

The finance ministry said on Thursday that total public debt rose to $10.348 billion at the end of December 1996 from $7.346 billion in January. Foreign debt rose to $1.769 billion from $1.305 billion over the same period.
The CGTL also said the government must cancel its four-year ban on public demonstrations.

The CGTL led street protests during a general strike on November 28 in protest against Hariri's ban on demonstrations, perceived failure to improve social conditions and a decision to close down scores of private radio and television stations.
